name: Madonna
hook: A dance-club regular whose second album, produced with a disco veteran, made her name a byword for pop reinvention.

blurb.age7: Madonna was a singer who became one of the most famous pop stars ever, and she kept changing her style again and again.
blurb.age13: Madonna Louise Ciccone broke through with 'Like a Virgin' (1984), produced by Chic's Nile Rodgers, and went on to reinvent her image and sound repeatedly across five decades, from dance-pop to electronic to whatever came next. She is also on this map because Weird Al parodied 'Like a Virgin' as 'Like a Surgeon' (1985), and this project takes its own name from that song.
blurb.adult: Madonna's career-long pattern of deliberate reinvention, rather than any single sound, is her defining trait, and 'Like a Virgin' (1984), produced by Nile Rodgers, established the template early: a dance record positioned as both provocation and pure pop craft. Her approval of Weird Al's 'Like a Surgeon' parody, unlike some artists' more complicated reactions to being parodied, was straightforward.

signatureTracks.title: Like a Virgin
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Produced by Nile Rodgers; the breakthrough that made her a permanent pop fixture and the direct target of Weird Al's 'Like a Surgeon'.

signatureTracks.title: Vogue
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Ballroom voguing brought into the pop mainstream, and a clean example of her recurring pattern of absorbing an underground scene into a hit single.
